The arrays are short so it'd unlikely to matter a ton, but we've already made a min-heap here so it should be fast. Except if we're not in heap mode..... Maybe that's a waste of time? It feels like a lot of code for what isn't the hot path. The hot path is really the `collect` method.

It's a min-heap so we could make something to do that iteration. It's finicky code that'd want its own unit test, probably randomized. But we totally could do it. If you leave the TODO I'll try and have a look. It may not be worth it. But it feels bad to ignore the heap property when sorting.

I know I didn't do it in `BucketedSort`, but could you please leave a javadoc describing the layout of this one? I believe it's something like "Each bucket reserves `bucketSize` slots. Each set of slots starts in "gather" mode and transitions to "heap" mode when it has `bucketSize` values added. When in "heap" mode the slots store the values in the heap. When in "gather" mode we fill slots from high index to low index, with the slot at the lowest heap index containing the count of values added to the set so far." I think an example or two may help to be honest. It's kind of a lot, and I came up with it years ago.
